answer: Each identity must complete a prescribed chain of modular squarings, where every result depends on the previous one; GPUs can run separate chains, but cannot split one chain to remove its sequential delay. Thus, creating many clones multiplies the work and imposes a real-time and hardware cost, rather than granting instant identities. A Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check completion efficiently, while the vault, ember, and grove labels do not bypass the timed computation.
